questions.stem: For exercise 1097 on the 10.94.0.0/16 network, consider how a packet network works. What is the correct interpretation of network address translation here?
questions.subject: COMPUTER_NETWORKS

questions.explanation: Network address translation conserves public addresses by letting many private hosts share one or a few external addresses. The translating device keeps a table of active mappings, usually including ports, so return traffic can be matched to the correct internal host. Because the mapping is stateful, replies in the opposite direction are handled differently from fresh outbound connections. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
questions.hint: Ask how a reply finds its way back to the right internal machine.
